newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK Q1 BUDGET PRODUCES SURPLUS OF 44 BLN DRS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK Q1 BUDGET PRODUCES SURPLUS OF 44 BLN DRS.

text.p: Greece's general government budget turned out a surplus of 44 billion drachmas ($161.3 million) in the first quarter of 1997, its first since 1991, versus a deficit of 386.2 billion in the same period in 1996, central bank figures showed.

The central government budget was in the red for 146 billion drachmas but social security funds, hospitals and local authorities produced a surplus of 190 billion drachmas in the first quarter to tip the balance, the figures showed.

Public enterprises reported a deficit of 7.0 billion drachmas in the first quarter bringing the public sector surplus down to 37 billion versus a deficit of 392.2 billion in the first quarter of 1996.

The net borrowing requirements of the public sector, measured on a cash basis, did not include capitalised and accrued interest, the Bank of Greece said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ($ = 272.7 Greek Drachmas)
